# contracts — agent brief

## Purpose
contracts is the platform's shared schema kernel. It defines every cross-hexagon port as OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema and generates Java, TypeScript and Python bindings that consumers pin by Git tag (D031).
It is not a service: no runtime, no business logic. It never fixes another repo; it raises a demand instead.
Description: [hexagon page](../documentations/reference/hexagons/contracts.md) · [HEXAGON.md](HEXAGON.md)

## Build, test, run
pip install jsonschema pyyaml
python tests/run_all.py
mvn -f $PWD/gen/java/pom.xml test | grep 'Tests run'
cd gen/ts && npm ci && npx tsc --noEmit
# regenerate bindings: per-language commands in DEPLOYMENT.md (python-regen-procedure)
# after pushing a tag: git worktree add --detach ../contracts-worktrees/vX.Y.Z vX.Y.Z

## Top gotchas
- **npx tsc resolves to a squatter package** — Never run npx tsc in a scratch project; install typescript there and use its tsc. In a scratch project, npx resolves 'tsc' to an unrelated squatter package, and the acceptance fails for no real reason. Inside gen/ts, npm ci installs typescript first, so npx tsc --noEmit is safe there. ([note](.brain/notes/npx-tsc-is-a-squatter.md))
- **mvn -f with a relative pom path runs no tests** — Call mvn -f with an absolute pom path and grep the 'Tests run' summary. With a relative path and the shell cwd somewhere else, mvn exits 1 without running a single test, and that is easy to miss. From the repo root: mvn -f $PWD/gen/java/pom.xml test | grep 'Tests run' ([note](.brain/notes/mvn-needs-absolute-pom-path.md))
- **CHANGELOG.md and gen/ts/index.ts are cp1252, index.ts is CRLF** — Edit CHANGELOG.md and gen/ts/index.ts as bytes (latin-1 round trip), not as UTF-8 text. Both files contain cp1252 bytes, so read and write them with encoding='latin-1'. gen/ts/index.ts also uses CRLF line endings: keep them. Its line 1 says v0.1.0, but that comment is stale and is not the version. ([note](.brain/notes/cp1252-and-crlf-files.md))
- **datamodel-codegen renumbers inline enums on every regen** — A regen can rename public Python enum classes (TaskWorkspaceState -> State1, Status1..N). datamodel-codegen numbers clashing inline enum names in definition order. A regen or a new inline enum can rename existing classes, which turns an additive release into a breaking one. Give new enums a named $defs entry and $ref it. Diff the generated module for renames and restore the old names by hand before committing. ([note](.brain/notes/python-regen-renames-enums.md))
